title: A trip — regular past
practiceFocus: Tell a short trip story using four verbs and persons

points.title: The full chart, from the day 13 chunks
points.rule: Day 13 only gave the yo form of a handful of verbs: comí, trabajé, cené. Now every person of a regular verb follows one of two patterns. -ar verbs use -é, -aste, -ó, -amos, -aron. -er and -ir verbs share -í, -iste, -ió, -imos, -ieron. Visitar and llegar follow viajar. Comer follows the same pattern as salir.

examples.english: comer, the same -er pattern as salir

grammar.notYet: Verbs that change spelling in the yo form (llegué, not llegé), and the irregular verbs from day 23.

phrases.spanish: Viajé a España el año pasado.
phrases.english: I travelled to Spain last year.
We arrived late at the airport.

phrases.spanish: Salieron del hotel a las ocho.
phrases.english: They left the hotel at eight.
We ate at a local restaurant.

phrases.spanish: Visitamos tres ciudades en una semana.
phrases.english: We visited three cities in one week.

dialogue.title: Telling a friend about the trip

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.spanish: Viajé a Portugal con mi familia. Visitamos Lisboa y Oporto.
lines.english: I travelled to Portugal with my family. We visited Lisbon and Porto.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.spanish: Sí. Llegamos tarde el primer día, pero después todo fue bien.
lines.english: Yes. We arrived late the first day, but after that everything was fine.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.spanish: Comimos mucho pescado. Salimos a caminar todas las tardes.
lines.english: We ate a lot of fish. We went out walking every afternoon.

practice.title: A short trip story
practice.instruction: Tell the story of a real or imagined trip in four or five sentences. Use viajé or viajamos, visité or visitamos, llegué or llegamos, and salí or salimos. Mix yo and nosotros, and add one él/ella or ellos sentence about someone else on the trip.
starters: Mi amigo/a llegó… / Mis amigos llegaron…
tips: Say the ending out loud before the whole sentence: -é or -amos, -í or -imos.
